title: Automated regression investigator for embedding + reranker telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated 'regression investigator' that ties model/config changes to measurable degradation in embedding + reranker offline metrics and drift signals, and surfaces actionable root-cause candidates for triage. This ticket implements the analysis pipeline, CI hooks, dashboarding, and runbook actions required to go from alert -> RCA -> mitigation for config- or model-triggered regressions.

Why: We still spend >2 engineer-days per incident manually correlating PRs/config changes with embedding drift and rerank recall drops. A lightweight investigator that attributes delta fingerprints to recent changes will reduce MTTR and enable safer automated rollouts.

Scope & approach:
- Data inputs: daily batch of production traffic samples (anonymized), canonical offline eval set (10k queries across major customer scenarios), synthetic probe set (perturbation variants for stability checks), recent model/config change metadata (git tags, config diffs, rollout IDs).
- Core analysis outputs: delta summary (delta recall@10, delta precision@1, delta MRR@10), embedding distance shift distribution (Cosine mean/median, KS p-value), feature-level attribution (which config flag or model param most correlated with drop using permutation importance + basic causal heuristics), and confidence score for likely root cause.
- Metrics & thresholds (initial): alert if offline recall@10 drops by >=2.5% absolute on canonical eval set OR if embedding distribution KS test p-value < 0.01 with mean cosine shift > 0.01. Secondary checks: precision@1 drop >=1.5% or MRR@10 drop >=2%.
- Investigation heuristics: prioritize changes in model weights (version bump), tokenizer/token config, embedding dimension/quantization flags, reranker hyperparams (temp, top-k candidate generator), and data preprocessing steps. Use delta fingerprints: pairwise attribute hashing of recent changes to attribute weight.
- CI integration: run investigator as a post-merge job for merges touching model/config directories and as nightly job. Post-merge failures create a regression alert PR comment and link to investigator output.
- Outputs & runbook: human-readable RCA summary, ranked suspects, suggested mitigations (rollback to previous model, re-run quantization with new params, add targeted eval probes), and automated rollback toggle for critical customers.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Investigator runs end-to-end in CI and on nightly batches, producing deterministic JSON report and Grafana link.
2) Alerts are triggered for the defined thresholds and include top-3 suspects and supporting metrics.
3) A triage runbook is attached to alerts with playbook actions and Slack escalation path.
4) Two internal demos completed (Eng + PM + Solutions) with feedback addressed.
5) Integration tests: create synthetic regression via model-changes in a staging job and prove investigator surfaces correct suspect within top-3.

Implementation notes & trade-offs:
- Start with offline deterministic analysis (no causal inference at scale) and conservative thresholds to avoid false positives. We may incrementally add Bayesian attribution later.
- Avoid heavy-weight model explainers (SHAP) initially because runtime and complexity; use permutation importance and change-frequency heuristics.
- Privacy: use sampled/anonymized token hashes and never persist raw PII. Coordinate with privacy team on sample retention.

Infra / dependencies:
- Needs access to daily traffic sample S3 path and anonymization job (Infra owns).
- Requires a lightweight runner in CI that can access build artifacts for model diffs.
- Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard and alert rule (ENG-33011 dependency for dashboard panels).

Risks:
- False positives from natural drift leading to alert fatigue. Mitigation: tune thresholds and require corroborating signals before auto-rollback.
- Attribution errors when multiple changes land together. Mitigation: prefer canary-triggered investigator runs and include time-windowed attribution.

Next steps:
1) Spike: prototype offline investigator on 30 days of historical incidents to validate heuristics (owner: Marco).
2) Build CI hook and JSON report schema (owner: Marco).
3) Implement Grafana panels and alert rules (owner: Observability eng).
4) Write runbook and demo to PM/SE teams (owner: Aisha).
